intro: The Litter-Robot 4 reports almost everything through its light bar, and both colour and pattern matter: solid red and flashing red mean different things. The meanings below follow Whisker's official light codes guide. Whisker revises codes with firmware updates, so if your unit shows something not listed here, their guide is the authority.

facts.text: Rated for cats from 3 to 25 lb; each cat must be at least 3 lb for Automatic Mode.
Whisker notes the scale is most accurate on a firm surface rather than carpet or uneven flooring.
Designed for standard-weight clay clumping litter. Whisker lists crystal, plant-based, wood pellet, newspaper and non-clumping litters as incompatible.
Runs on a 15 V DC power supply. Using the wrong supply triggers its own light code.

symptoms.title: Flashing blue light
symptoms.summary: A flashing blue light bar means the waste drawer is full.

fixes.detail: Empty the waste drawer, press Reset, then press Cycle.

symptoms.escalate: If it keeps flashing blue with an empty drawer, Whisker's drawer-full guide and support line are the next step.

symptoms.title: Blue with two flashing yellow lights
symptoms.summary: The scale has been triggered for more than 30 minutes.
causes: Something is resting on or against the unit, or the base is not sitting squarely on the floor.

fixes.detail: Remove anything adding weight, and make sure the unit is not on carpet, a litter mat, a power cord or a grout line, and is not touching a wall. Then press Reset.

symptoms.escalate: If the alert returns with the unit clear and level, contact Whisker — the scale may need attention.

symptoms.title: Solid red light
symptoms.summary: The cat sensor has detected a cat entering, and the cycle delay countdown has started.

fixes.detail: The unit cycles once the countdown ends. Pressing Reset starts the cycle sooner.

symptoms.escalate: Solid red that never clears after the countdown is not normal — check for the flashing red condition below.

symptoms.title: Flashing red light
symptoms.summary: A cat or weight has been detected in the globe for more than 30 minutes.
causes: A cat is resting inside, or litter, a toy or another object is weighing on the sensor.

fixes.detail: Make sure no cat is inside and nothing is sitting in the globe or leaning on the unit. Whisker links a dedicated guide for this code from its light codes page.

symptoms.escalate: If it flashes red with the globe empty and nothing touching the unit, follow Whisker's red flashing guide or contact their support.

symptoms.title: Red with two flashing yellow lights
symptoms.summary: The globe is jammed or overloaded. The motor stops, retracts and tries to continue the cycle.
causes: Too much litter, or a large clump, is resisting rotation.

fixes.detail: Bring the litter down to the fill line and remove any large clump, then let the unit retry.

symptoms.escalate: Repeated jams on a correct litter level point to a mechanical problem. Contact Whisker rather than forcing the globe.

symptoms.title: Solid yellow light
causes: A button press or interruption paused the cycle.

fixes.detail: Press Cycle or Reset. If neither resumes it, turn the unit off with the Power button and back on.

symptoms.escalate: If it will not leave the paused state after a power cycle, contact Whisker.

symptoms.title: Flashing yellow light
causes: The bonnet is off or not seated.

fixes.detail: Replace the bonnet. The unit resumes what it was doing about five seconds later.

symptoms.escalate: Flashing yellow with the bonnet firmly in place suggests a sensor problem worth raising with Whisker.

symptoms.title: One yellow light moving back and forth
symptoms.summary: The pinch detector has been activated.
causes: Something has triggered the anti-pinch protection during movement.

fixes.detail: Look for anything caught between the globe and the base before restarting.

symptoms.escalate: If the pinch detector keeps tripping with nothing in the way, contact Whisker.

symptoms.title: Red and blue alternating
symptoms.summary: The three laser curtain sensors need cleaning.
causes: Litter dust on the curtain sensors.

fixes.detail: Clean the three laser sensors that detect a cat at the entrance.

symptoms.escalate: If the alert persists after cleaning, Whisker can walk through recalibration.

symptoms.title: Green with two flashing red lights
symptoms.summary: Automatic calibration of the cat-detection sensors has failed and they need cleaning.

fixes.detail: Clean the sensors. A green light moving back and forth afterwards means calibration is running and needs nothing from you.

symptoms.escalate: If calibration keeps failing on clean sensors, contact Whisker.

symptoms.title: Wi-Fi light by the Connect button
symptoms.summary: The small light beside the Connect button shows the network state separately from the main light bar.
causes: Flashing blue: connecting, or trying to reconnect after losing the connection.
Flashing red: the unit cannot reach the router.
Solid white: Wi-Fi is switched off.

fixes.detail: Check the router is on and working, then power cycle the robot.
Short-press the Connect button to turn Wi-Fi back on.

symptoms.escalate: Whisker lists a flashing white Wi-Fi light as a defective Wi-Fi chip, which means a base replacement through support.

symptoms.title: Red and green alternating
symptoms.summary: The unit has lost its factory scale calibration.
causes: A scale calibration fault in the base.

fixes.detail: This is not user-fixable: Whisker states the base needs replacing. Submit a support request.

symptoms.escalate: Contact Whisker support directly for a base replacement.

symptoms.title: Solid purple light
causes: Sleep Mode was enabled, by schedule or by hand.

fixes.detail: Long-press the Cycle button to turn Sleep Mode off, or back on.

symptoms.escalate: If it will not leave Sleep Mode, check the schedule in the Whisker app.

symptoms.title: Clumps break up or litter leaves residue
symptoms.summary: Cycles leave waste behind, clumps crumble, or litter collects where it should not.
causes: The litter is not one Whisker recommends for this unit.

fixes.detail: Use a high-quality, standard-weight clay clumping litter. Whisker lists crystal, plant-based, wood pellet, newspaper and non-clumping litters as incompatible.

symptoms.escalate: If problems continue on a recommended litter, work through the light codes above or contact Whisker.
